t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Edmundo of Endsmeet was listed as senator for Zenith.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Mentioned in passing: the Great Pits of Ennerlund were listed as held by Vasiliy Krenyenkov Valeskai Strascovich, for a bid of 370 Thrones.

Assignment of Mournwold.d: The motion to assign Mournwold to the Marches was proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by the senator for Mitwold, and it passed. As a result Mournwold formally became part of the Marches, which meant the territory could elect a senator to represent it in the Senate.

n.The Marches: The Marches formally gained Mournwold as one of its territories, at the instigation of its own senators for Bregasland and Mitwold.

t.Mournwold: Mournwold was assigned to the Marches and could now elect its own senator.

Birds and bats.d: Lashonar's herald delivered a sonnet proposing a contest of real love letters, open to anyone whose name was placed in a vessel in the Hall of Worlds; Rossignol would visit those named at Anvil. Sadogua, distressed at losing the Empire's amity, sent Neora of Spiral, a young girl with a potent naga lineage, to request a parley under the Archmage of Night. He wished to discuss saving the Halls of Knowledge from the Druj, offer to reforge or restore rare items he had given Imperial magicians, ask about a certain weirwood tree, and discuss the Dark Moon legacy. The parley took place on Saturday night; its content stayed private, but after the Winter Solstice the Halls of Knowledge vanished from Zenith, whether through a deal with Sadogua or Druj machinations.

n.Druj: Sadogua framed his parley around saving the Halls of Knowledge from the Druj, and their later disappearance may have been the result of some Druj machination.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's young naga-blooded messenger gave her name as Neora of Spiral, a territory held by the Grendel.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the in-character fiction features Richard of Holberg, a Leaguer, trying to explain to Sadogua why the Conclave was displeased with him.
n.Urizen: The Halls of Knowledge in Urizen's territory of Zenith, which Sadogua claimed he could help save from the Druj, vanished mysteriously shortly after the Winter Solstice.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg appears only in the name of Richard of Holberg, a character in the opening fiction.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's messenger introduced herself as Neora of Spiral.
t.Zenith: The Halls of Knowledge vanished from Zenith under mysterious circumstances shortly after the Winter Solstice, possibly through an arrangement with Sadogua or Druj machinations.

Construct Giant's Well.d: The motion called for a folly in Mitwold in the Marches, consisting of a white granite standing stone placed over the site known as the Giant's Well. It was passed in principle in Autumn 381YE and was to be self-funded. The minimum cost was 5 wains of white granite and 10 crowns in labour, with construction taking three months. William Guildenstern provided the granite and the crowns after the Autumn Equinox 381YE. The menhir, which came to be known as the Pale Chain, now covers the Giant's Well.

n.The Marches: The Marches gained a new landmark when Mitwold's own senator saw the Giant's Well capped with a white granite standing stone, the Pale Chain, paid for by William Guildenstern.

t.Mitwold: The Giant's Well in Mitwold is now covered by the Pale Chain, a white granite menhir raised as a folly over the site.

Construct Honour's Rest.d: Proposed by Kallavesa's senator and seconded by Volodmartz's, the motion would construct the congregational sinecure Honour's Rest in Overton, in the Greensward region of the Mournwold. Once completed it would create the title Friar of Honour's Rest, appointed by the Marcher National Assembly and revocable in the usual way. Wintermark was to fund the work itself as a gift, and Olle Markusson provided 16 wains of white granite and 4 thrones after the Autumn Equinox 381YE. The motion passed in principle, but no construction progress is recorded.

n.The Marches: The Marcher National Assembly would gain the right to appoint the Friar of Honour's Rest once the sinecure in their Mournwold territory is completed.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's people undertook to fund the sinecure themselves as a gift to the Mournwold. Olle Markusson supplied the white granite and thrones, and the senators of Kallavesa and Volodmartz proposed and seconded the motion.

t.Mournwold: The Marcher-held Mournwold was to receive a new congregational sinecure in Overton, given by Wintermark as an acknowledgement that the Empire makes mistakes.

r.Mournwold/Greensward: Honour's Rest was to be built at Overton in the Greensward, though no progress on its construction is recorded.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition.d: Proposed by the senator for Karov and seconded by the senator for Tassato, the motion commissioned a great work using the skills of the Asavean Architect, overseen by Almodin Oktístis, Priest of the Builder. It cost 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones, to be funded by the Bloody Butchers Bank, and took three months to complete. The materials and money were provided by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar. Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition was finished in Tassato shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE and provides 37 crystal mana each season, shared among the citizens of Tassato who own a mana site.

n.The League: League mana site owners in Tassato gain a share of 37 extra crystal mana each season, from a great work paid for by the League's Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar and the Bloody Butchers Bank.

t.Tassato: Lorenzo's Legacy of Ambition now stands in Tassato, completed before the Winter Solstice 381YE and providing 37 crystal mana each season to the territory's mana site owners.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Courage.d: Announced in Autumn 381YE by Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar under the construction powers the Senate delegates to holders of an Imperial Wayleave, the great work cost 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones and took three months to build. The text said it would be funded by the Bloody Butchers Guild, and the materials were provided by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar. Lorenzo's Legacy of Courage was finished in Holberg shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE. It provides 37 crystal mana each season, shared among the citizens of Holberg who own a mana site.

n.The League: A League citizen paid for a great work in a League city, and the League's mana-site owners in Holberg gain a lasting yearly supply of crystal mana from it.

t.Holberg: Holberg is now home to Lorenzo's Legacy of Courage, which yields 37 crystal mana each season, divided among the territory's mana site owners.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Zenith, the motion commissioned the Asavean architect, with the work overseen by Almodin Oktístis, Priest of the Builder, to construct a great work for the production of mana in Temeschwar. It cost 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones, intended to be funded by the Bloody Butchers Bank, and took three months to complete. The materials and money were provided by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar. Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty was completed shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE and provides 37 crystal mana each season, shared among the citizens of Temeschwar who own a mana site.

n.The League: A League citizen, Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar, paid for the great work, and League mana-site owners in Temeschwar gain a share of 37 crystal mana each season.

t.Temeschwar: Lorenzo's Legacy of Loyalty was built in Temeschwar shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE, and it provides 37 crystal mana each season to the territory's mana-site owners.

Construct Lorenzo's Legacy of Pride.d: Announced by Silas di Sarvos using the Senate's delegated power to commission constructions under an Imperial Wayleave, the great work cost 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones and took three months to build. The commission named the Bloody Butchers Guild as the funder, and the materials and money were supplied by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar. Lorenzo's Legacy of Pride was finished in Sarvos shortly before the Winter Solstice 381YE. It provides 37 crystal mana each season, shared among those citizens of Sarvos who own a mana site.

n.The League: League magicians who own mana sites in Sarvos now share an extra 37 crystal mana each season, paid for by a League benefactor, Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos gained the great work Lorenzo's Legacy of Pride, completed before the Winter Solstice 381YE, which adds 37 crystal mana each season for the territory's mana site owners.

Construct Mountains of the Moon spy netw.d: In Autumn 381YE the Senate considered a motion to construct a spy network in the area called the Valley of the Moon, which the Axou know as the Valley of Silence. The target lay in the Mountains of the Moon, an unknown territory east of Urizen. Casinea proposed the motion and Therunin seconded it. Standard costs would have applied had it passed. The motion failed, so no spy network was built and the Empire gained no new means of observing the region.

n.Urizen: Urizen's eastern neighbour, the Mountains of the Moon, stays unobserved, because the motion to place a spy network across its eastern border failed.

t.Mountains of the Moon: No Imperial spy network was built in the Valley of the Moon, so the Tsark-held territory remained beyond the Empire's watch.

Construct Treasure Ship.d: Proposed by Madruga and seconded by Morrow, the motion was raised on behalf of Solomon, Archmage of Summer, to win the support of Rhianos, Regent of the Eternal Sea. Once completed, the Adventure would leave the Bay of Catazar with any fleets willing to accompany it. It would seek the fiercest tempest, where its crew would lash the wheel, steer it towards the eye of the storm and scuttle it, sending ship and cargo to the deep before boarding the escorting vessels. The motion passed. Anwar i Del Toro i Riquezza provided 3 wains of mithril, 3 wains of weirwood and 12 crowns towards its construction. The outcome of the venture is unknown.

t.Bay of Catazar: The treasure ship Adventure was to set sail from the Bay of Catazar, leaving it behind with any accompanying fleets, before seeking out a tempest to be scuttled in.

Construct mana sinecure at New Dunhall.d: Using the Senate's delegated power to commission constructions, Breeta Dunning announced a sinecure at New Dunhall (given as New Dunholm in the announcement) in Hahnmark. Its purpose was to cultivate and collect the mana crystallisations forming around the newly opened hole, Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, for the prosperity of Wintermark. The work was self-funded, costing 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns, and was to take three months. Balder supplied the materials and money after the Autumn Equinox 381YE. Completing the sinecure would create a new Imperial title, Fallsheart Guardian, whose details and method of appointment were left for Breeta Dunning to determine.

n.Wintermark: The sinecure was explicitly intended to increase Wintermark's prosperity by harvesting mana in one of its own territories, and it would create a new Imperial title, the Fallsheart Guardian.

t.Hahnmark: New Dunhall in Hahnmark was to gain a sinecure overseeing the mana crystallising around Lorenzo's Deep Pockets, with construction funded after the Autumn Equinox and due to take three months.

Construct south west road network.d: Proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Kallavesa in Autumn 381YE, the motion described the network as partly self-funded. It would run from Anduz in Segura through Madruga to Tassato, needing 80 wains of white granite, 20 thrones of labour and six months to build. After the Winter Solstice, Lorenzo “La Volpe” Macelliao von Temeschwar gave the 20 thrones and Qusay i Kalamar i Guerra gave 20 wains of white granite. Qusay supplied the remaining 60 wains after the Spring Equinox, covering the full cost. Once complete, the great work will raise the income of farms and businesses in Segura and Madruga.

n.The Brass Coast: Two Brass Coast territories, Segura and Madruga, lie along the road and stand to gain higher farm and business income once the great work is finished.
n.The League: The League's territory of Tassato is the far end of the planned road, which will connect it to Anduz in Segura.

t.Madruga: The road will pass through Madruga, and once it is complete, farms and businesses there will earn more.
t.Segura: The road will start at Anduz in Segura, and once it is complete, farms and businesses in the territory will earn more.
t.Tassato: Tassato is the destination of the road network. The page lists no direct income benefit for the territory itself.

Construct the Weaver's Market.d: Proposed by Sarvos and seconded by Redoubt, the motion called for a mana ministry in Skarsind, appointed in the usual way for an Imperial Orc National Bourse position. Construction required at least 12 wains of mithril, 3 Thrones in labour costs and three months of work. The mithril and Thrones were provided after the Autumn Equinox 381YE. Once built, the ministry created the Imperial title of Four Seasons' Boneweaver, appointed by Imperial Orcs who own a military unit, giving its holder access to purchases of crystal mana.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs gained a national ministry, the Four Seasons' Boneweaver, which is appointed by Imperial Orcs who command a military unit and gives them a means to buy crystal mana.

t.Skarsind: The weavers' market mana ministry was to be built in Skarsind, and the 12 wains of mithril and 3 Thrones needed for its construction were supplied after the Autumn Equinox.

Create title of Keeper of the Breadbaske.d: Proposed by the senator for Upwold and seconded by the senator for Mournwold, the motion created a national title chosen by the Marcher senators for a one-year term and revocable by the Marcher Assembly or the Assembly of Nine. The Keeper maintains the Great Work and may decide, once per summit, whether the Breadbasket supports the Mournwold or the Imperial armies, including which army benefits. Decisions are made by announcement. The title also carries a right of address to the Senate once per summit, but the Constitution's review noted that the motion's attempt to require that address be used when changing the allocation was unconstitutional. The motion passed.

n.The Marches: The Marches gained a new national title, appointed by their senators and answerable to the Marcher Assembly or the Assembly of Nine, which gives a Marcher custody of the Imperial Breadbasket and control over where its benefits go.

t.Mournwold: The Mournwold's senator seconded the motion, and the new Keeper decides whether the Breadbasket's granaries and storehouses support the Mournwold or are directed to the Imperial armies instead.

Desperate affairs, desperate measures.d: Slightly more than thirty Imperial captains guarded the fisherfolk exploiting a boom in marine life. Each protecting fleet earned an extra 3 Crowns, trade rose in several territories, and the Broken Shore Bounty will yield 2 extra rings of ilium a season for a year. Fifty fleets, thirty of them Freeborn, broke the blockade of Zemress and carried its people and livestock to Joharra. The islanders' leader, Dhomiro Tevus i Zemress, burned the village behind them. The Grendel pirates withdrew in disarray. The Islanders, who are Freeborn but distinct, wished to settle together. Feroz, Madruga, Segura and Kahraman were all weighed, and a statement upheld with a greater majority chose Segura.

n.Grendel: Grendel pirates and slavers were beaten off at both the fishing grounds and Zemress, and their independent captains withdrew in disarray. They remain a threat to individual ships, but no longer act in concert.
n.Highguard: Highborn captains joined the fishing-fleet defence and the Zemress evacuation, and trade in Necropolis increased as a result.
n.Imperial Orcs: An Imperial Orc fleet captained by Gish was among the scattering of non-Freeborn ships that helped rescue the Zemress Islanders.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Islanders were suggested as a possible bulwark should the Jotun come down from Liathaven or Lasambria again.
n.Navarr: More than half a dozen Navarr fleets supported the Zemress evacuation, and many Navarr captains took part in the campaign against the pirates.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn led the campaign, providing thirty ships for the Zemress raid, and gained several thousand kin who settled first in Feroz and Madruga. Their Assembly directed the Islanders to Segura.
n.The League: League captains from Sarvos joined the action, and trade in Sarvos and Tassato increased thanks to the protected fishing fleet.
n.Urizen: Urizen fleets, including that of Natalus, took part in the operations, and trade in Redoubt rose as a result.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark captains such as Pendraed the Maker, Drothdir and Kapik joined the Imperial fleets that defied the Grendel and rescued the Islanders.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Empire's fleets kept the fishing grounds safe and drove the organised Grendel pirate fleet out of these waters, though lone raiders remain a danger.
t.Feroz: Trade increased here thanks to the protected fishing fleet, and many rescued Islanders arrived here. Feroz was considered as their permanent home but not chosen.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman was considered as a home for the Islanders, with its mines and grazing land, but the Assembly chose Segura instead.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: named as a place from which the Jotun might again descend on Kahraman.
t.Madruga: Madruga saw increased trade and received many of the rescued Islanders. It was weighed as a permanent home but passed over in favour of Segura.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis enjoyed a significant increase in trade as a result of the successful defence of the fishing fleet.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt saw a significant rise in trade thanks to the fishing fleet's safe harvest.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos benefited from a significant increase in trade following the protection of the fishing fleet.
t.Segura: The Freeborn Assembly encouraged the several thousand Zemress Islanders to settle in Segura. Their hard work may help revitalise a territory still recovering from conquest and strengthen its defence.
t.Tassato: Tassato enjoyed a significant increase in trade from the safeguarded fishing fleet.

r.Feroz/Morajasse: Morajasse was suggested as a place where settling Islanders could aid the herb-growing apothecaries, though Segura was chosen instead.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Oranseri was flagged as somewhere to keep the Islanders away from, given how the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull might react to their worship.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Braydon's Jasse was proposed as a defensive settlement site in the shadow of Fort Braydon on the Marches border. The option was not taken up.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: The Jade Range was suggested as rich grazing ground where Islander ranchers could ease Kahraman's dependence on imported food. Segura was chosen instead.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Zemress herself was born in Calvos, and the Kraken's Bane rests on its dock, a touchstone the Islanders will likely want to visit.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page, but it lies in Segura, where the Assembly encouraged the Islanders to settle.
r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: The Sobral Grasses were suggested as a place for the Islanders to raise herds and establish farms within their chosen territory of Segura.
r.Segura/Yellow Chase: Yellow Chase was named as a possible site for Islander herds and farms that could raise the prosperity of Segura.

Disburse funds for Astolat ministry.d: The senator for Astolat proposed a motion requesting funds for a mana ministry in Astolat, and the senator for Weirwater seconded it. The motion passed, and the disbursement was approved at a cost of 40 Thrones. The page gives no further detail about the ministry itself, its location within Astolat or how it would be run.

n.Dawn: Dawnish senators for Astolat and Weirwater proposed and seconded the motion, securing Imperial funds for a mana ministry in one of Dawn's own territories.

t.Astolat: Astolat's senator successfully sought 40 Thrones for a mana ministry to be established in the territory.

Empty handed.d: Ellie West of Mitwold brought a crystal full of Autumn magic to sell, seeking the Bailiff of the Grand Market and the Hall of Worlds. Earl Celeste offered Circe's Necklace, a cursed but potent talisman, to Dawn's troubadours for 25 thrones, to be borne each year by a worthy Dawnish citizen. After Seneca of Zenith burned his garden before the Druj and was killed, Sadogua offered the silent gardener and Seneca's tea recipe to whichever tea-house gave him the most dragonbone. Orc apothecary Youngtongue brought unknown potions and a Hungry Key to sell. Varushka held its Winter Market, and Senator Llewellyn Leafstalker convened an Imperial Conference on Economics.

n.Dawn: Earl Celeste of the faded House Magot offered Circe's Necklace to the troubadours of Dawn for 25 thrones, to be awarded yearly to the citizen who best exemplifies Dawn's glorious traditions, though it carries a non-fatal curse.
n.Druj: Druj forces overran parts of Zenith and caught and killed the magician Seneca as he fled, though he had already burned the herb garden they would have coveted; they had also killed Youngtongue's brother when the orcs fled the Barrens.
n.Navarr: Navarr senator Llewellyn Leafstalker convened an Imperial Conference on Economics in response to the Bourse crash, and the Bitterbark tea-house was named among those likely to bid for the silent gardener.
n.The Marches: Young Ellie West carried an Autumn-magic crystal from Mitwold to Anvil to sell, and half the proceeds of the economics conference's ticket auction were promised to a Marcher cause chosen by Merrick's, which hosted the conference.
n.Urizen: Urizeni magicians in Zenith destroyed their life's work rather than let the Druj take it, including Seneca's prized tea garden, and the Sentinel's Repose was named as a natural bidder to inherit the silent gardener's aid.
n.Varushka: Varushkans held their Winter Market in Anvil, where hearth magic compels anyone treated as a trader to act as one, followed by a Night Market of storytelling and entertainment.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Lumis tea-house in Wintermark was named as likely to be interested in bidding for the silent gardener.

t.Mitwold: A crystal thought to be a fallen star was found near the Westmere, drawing landskeepers and beaters to the West household before Ellie West took it to Anvil to sell.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: Youngtongue's brother was killed fighting the Druj when the Great Forest Orcs fled the Barrens.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest Orcs now living in Therunin sent Youngtongue to Anvil, with his elders' leave, to sell his dead brother's potions and Hungry Key and raise coin for their people there.
t.Zenith: As the Druj overran parts of Zenith, the Spire of the Dark Moon's tea-house garden was burned by Seneca, who was then caught and killed while fleeing.

Fortify Freemoor.d: Proposed by Miekarova and seconded by Temeschwar, the motion called for a new fortification in Freemoor, at the standard cost of 80 wains of white granite and 20 thrones, taking a year to build with an upkeep of 10 thrones. Nikolovich Drakov supplied 29 wains of white granite after the Winter Solstice 381YE and 16 thrones after the Spring Equinox 382YE. The Silent Sentinel opportunity effectively provided another 16 wains and 4 thrones. Landon of Longridge gave 15 wains and Orrick of House Bolholt gave 20 more over 383YE, which met the full cost. The fortification of Landskeepers Bulwark was then completed.

n.The Marches: The Marches, which held the Mournwold at the time, gained Landskeepers Bulwark as a new fortification on their land in Freemoor.

t.Mournwold: The Mournwold, then held by the Marches, gained a new fortification, Landskeepers Bulwark, built after several years of contributions of granite and thrones.

r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Freemoor is where Landskeepers Bulwark was built, and it now stands complete in the region.

Fortify Greensward.d: The motion was proposed by the Conscience of the Senate and seconded by Holberg. It called for a rank one fortification costing 80 wains of white granite and 20 Thrones, taking a year to build, with upkeep of 10 Thrones. Orrick provided 40 wains of white granite after the Winter Solstice 381YE. The Silent Sentinel opportunity effectively contributed 16 wains of white granite and 32 crowns. Orrick then supplied the remaining 24 wains and 16 Thrones after the Spring Equinox 382YE. Farstrider's Watch was due for completion shortly before the Winter Solstice 382YE.

n.The Marches: The Marches gained a new rank one fortification, Farstrider's Watch, to strengthen the defence of their Mournwold lands.

t.Mournwold: Mournwold, held by the Marches, was to receive its new fortification of Farstrider's Watch, due for completion shortly before the Winter Solstice 382YE.

r.Mournwold/Greensward: The Greensward was the chosen site for Farstrider's Watch, a new rank one fortification built with white granite supplied largely by Orrick.

Fortify Lower Tarn Valley.d: Proposed by Redoubt and seconded by Segura, the motion arose from an opportunity offered by the Great Forest orcs. It would have cost 80 wains of weirwood and 20 thrones, taken a year, and not counted against the Senate's limited commissions. The orcs would garrison and control the rank one fortification, so the Empire would pay no upkeep. Constitutionally this amounted to ceding the fortification, though not the region, to the orcs. If the treaty broke and the orcs took the region, the Holt could support them against the Empire. Only 10 wains of weirwood, from Cybi Farkas, arrived after the Winter Solstice 381YE, so no work began before the commission lapsed.

n.Navarr: The motion would have placed an orc-controlled fortification inside Navarr's territory of Therunin, ceding the stronghold, though not the land, to the Great Forest orcs. The commission lapsed before any work was done.

t.Therunin: Therunin would have gained a rank one weirwood fortification garrisoned by the Great Forest orcs, which could have turned against Imperial forces if the treaty were broken. It was never built because too little weirwood arrived.

r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Lower Tarn Valley was the planned site of the Holt of the Oak, but only 10 wains of weirwood were delivered and the commission lapsed after the Autumn Equinox 382YE.

Fortify Southmoor.d: In Autumn 381YE a motion was put before the Senate to construct a new fortification in the region of Southmoor in the Mournwold. It was proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by the senator for Miekarova. The motion failed, so no fort was commissioned in Southmoor as a result of it. The page records no further details of the vote or any debate surrounding it.

n.Jotun: Jotun, which held the Mournwold at the time, faced no new Imperial fortification in Southmoor because the motion failed.
n.The Marches: The Marches, whose people sought to reclaim the Mournwold, did not gain a new Imperial fort in Southmoor to support that effort, as the motion failed.

t.Mournwold: The proposal to raise a new fortification in the Mournwold's Southmoor region came to nothing when the Senate rejected it.

r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Southmoor was the intended site of the proposed fort, but the motion's failure meant no fortification was commissioned there.

Hunters and wolves.d: A draughir messenger reached the Castle of Thorns with a letter from Exquy, herald of Sorin the Hungry Wolf. It invited nominations, placed in a locked box in the Hall of Worlds, for a trial of hard choices and suffering. Sorin's agent Ania of Necropolis would choose a few to face the first trial at the Winter Solstice. In Birchland three chained heralds of Tharim emerged from the Copse of the Bone Birch, claiming the Conclave's sanction. Two vanished into the woods and one, Obligatus, sat motionless on a stump for two months. Meanwhile magistrates traced mutilated corpses in Skarsind and Wintermark to a deranged devotee of Agramant, the Hahnmark strangler, who was caught, tried and executed. The Varushkan and Wintermark assemblies affirmed their alliance.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is not named on the page, whose events take place in Upwold, Hahnmark, Skarsind and at Anvil.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Sorin's draughir messenger was at first assumed to carry messages from Highguard senators, and his agent is Ania of Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: Lurid reports of mutilated corpses in the orcs' territory of Skarsind were traced to Agramant's fanatic, who has since been executed.
n.The Marches: Three heralds of Tharim appeared among the Marcher coven in Birchland and claimed the Conclave's sanction. One stayed seated in the regio under Landskeeper Benjamin Bickwoll's watchful eye.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan National Assembly declared the mutilations the work of a common enemy and stood with Wintermark, and the attempt to divide the two nations failed conclusively.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's people were the target of the Hahnmark strangler's killings and defilements, meant to set them against Varushka. The Wintermark Assembly unanimously reaffirmed its alliance with Varushka.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat is not named on the page.
t.Hahnmark: A militia patrol in Hahnmark caught the strangler carrying severed heads beside a ditch full of bodies, ending the series of killings meant to sow distrust.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Sorin's human agent, who would interview nominees for the trials, is named as Ania of Necropolis.
t.Skarsind: Reports of mutilated corpses in Skarsind were investigated by Imperial magistrates and attributed to the Agramant devotee, now executed.
t.Upwold: Heralds of Tharim emerged from a Winter regio in Upwold. Two disappeared into the woods heading north and east, while the third, Obligatus, remained.

r.Upwold/Birchland: Near Bickwoll, the heralds interrupted the ceremonial watering of the birch trees at the Copse of the Bone Birch. Obligatus sat motionless on a stump there for two months, and Landskeeper Benjamin Bickwoll may answer messages about it.

More love, less paperwork.d: La Volpe, Master of the Butchers Bank of Temeschwar, funded the Blood Red Roads, the Colossus of Sarvos and three blood-red places of pilgrimage in Temeschwar, Sarvos and Tassato. The General Assembly passed a mandate sending Jonah Yakovitch with 25 liao, so the faithful helped finish the roads' first leg just before the Winter Solstice 381YE rather than at Spring 382YE. A planned second phase would link Meade, Kalpaheim, Seren, Delev and Siroc. Irada von Temechwar's League Assembly mandate to recognise the monuments as inspiring all virtues, which would also have opened a similar great work in Holberg, was not upheld. The Druj destruction of The Gate in Semmerholm left one leg of the roads exposed. Astrid von Tassato consecrated the Colossus after Spring 383YE.

n.Dawn: The Druj invasion of Semmerholm and the destruction of The Gate put the Blood Red Roads through Dawnish land at risk. Losing Estmure could reduce the economic benefits the roads bring to Semmerholm.
n.Druj: The Druj invasion of Semmerholm and their destruction of The Gate were the one obstacle the roadbuilders could not overcome. Conquering Estmure would cut Holberg off from the rest of the Empire.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Seren in Miaren is named as one of the cities La Volpe plans to connect in the roads' second phase.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Siroc in Madruga is named as one of the cities La Volpe plans to connect in the roads' second phase.
n.The League: La Volpe's roads, Colossus and blood-red monuments shaped all four League cities, and the General Assembly hastened the roads' completion. The League Assembly failed to uphold the mandate recognising the monuments as inspiring every virtue, though the Colossus was later consecrated by Astrid von Tassato.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Meade in Mitwold is named as one of the cities La Volpe plans to connect in the roads' second phase.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Delev in Karov is named as one of the cities La Volpe plans to connect in the roads' second phase.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Kalpaheim in Hahnmark is named as one of the cities La Volpe plans to connect in the roads' second phase.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: its city of Kalpaheim is a proposed destination for the second phase of the Blood Red Roads.
t.Holberg: The roads reached Holberg through The Gate, now destroyed by the Druj, so a Druj conquest of Estmure would cut Holberg off from their benefits. A blood-red great work offered there depended on the League Assembly mandate, which failed.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: its city of Delev is a proposed destination for the second phase of the Blood Red Roads.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: its city of Siroc is a proposed destination for the second phase of the Blood Red Roads.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: its city of Seren is a proposed destination for the second phase of the Blood Red Roads.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: its city of Meade is a proposed destination for the second phase of the Blood Red Roads.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos is home to the Colossus and the Blood Red Quays art gallery, and Astrid von Tassato consecrated the Colossus after Spring 383YE. Consecration was said to raise the coin the Colossus gives Sarvos businesses from 900 to 1350 rings a season.
t.Semmerholm: The Druj invaded Semmerholm and destroyed The Gate on the road to Holberg, leaving that leg of the Blood Red Roads precarious. It also threatened the economic benefits the roads bring to the territory.
t.Tassato: Tassato's Blood Red River museum was among the monuments the failed League mandate would have made inspirational regardless of virtue. Astrid von Tassato later consecrated the Colossus.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar is home to La Volpe, the Butchers Bank and the Bloody Great Theatre, the origin of the building works that are reshaping the League.

r.Semmerholm/Estmure: Estmure became the key to the roads' Holberg leg: a Druj conquest here would cut Holberg off from the Empire and from the roads' benefits.

Out of void, out of chaos.d: Across the Empire, people dreamt of profound personal change and impossible things. For the Equinox, Distil the Serpent's Stone produced shadow eggs instead of serpent's stones. These eggs grant a temporary boost of six effective ranks of realm lore for a single ritual, but cannot cure poisons, lift curses or transform materials. Transmogrification of the Soul's Echo was enhanced, allowing targets to shed or gain naga lineage, change skills, or forget whole categories of rituals or recipes. Heralds of Murit and Soghter concluded their arrangements and vanished, apart from Centimani and Alkahest at Anvil. Their regio were sealed, and the eternals could not be contacted.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: enchanters in Dawn are among the magicians who reported that the heralds of Murit and Soghter were disappearing.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the 'incident in the Mournwold', a Marcher territory, is cited as the point since which the heralds of the two eternals have been conspicuously absent.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizeni Stargazers are among the magicians who reported the vanishing of Murit's and Soghter's heralds.

t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: an incident in the Mournwold is named as the moment after which heralds of Murit and Soghter all but disappeared.

Permit Great Forest Orcs to work the Thi.d: Proposed by the senator for Therunin and seconded by Karov, the motion answered an offer from the orcs of the Great Forest to tend the Thimble's weirwood groves. In return the orcs receive four wains of weirwood each season. The agreement lasts until the treaty with the Great Forest Orcs ends or the motion is revoked. The motion passed, and as a result the Great Forest Orcs work the Thimble, removing the cost to the Empire of maintaining that Bourse resource.

n.Navarr: Navarr's senator for Therunin proposed the motion, handing the work of the weirwood groves in a Navarr territory to the Great Forest Orcs in return for a share of the timber.

t.Therunin: The Thimble, Therunin's weirwood groves, is now worked by the Great Forest Orcs, who take four wains of weirwood each season while the Empire no longer bears the cost of its upkeep.

Praise and blame.d: Any of the Varushkan, Navarri, Highborn, Urizen or Dawnish assemblies could send a priest with 50 doses of liao to unlock the ruthless onslaught order, which raises casualties on both sides by a fifth. With 100 liao and 30 wains of mithril, three armies could also be permanently changed. The Eastern Sky could become bloodthirsty to avenge Druj ravages in Semmerholm. The Seventh Wave could become vengeful, remembering the Druj sack of Reikos. The Citadel Guard could trade cyclic magic for arcane mastery and its devastating Storm of Curses. Brat Umbral Path and Belakov Prochnost raised the ruthlessness mandates but neither was upheld. Sophus Cascade's Citadel Guard mandate was upheld, but after Lucretius died, Zeno, Stallion's Sibling, declined it. The opportunities have now lapsed.

n.Dawn: Dawn's assembly had already endorsed cruel armies, which opened the ruthless onslaught mandate. It also had a chance to make the Eastern Sky permanently bloodthirsty in revenge for the Druj invasion of Semmerholm, but the resolution records no Dawnish mandate taking effect.
n.Druj: The Druj invasion is the provocation behind every opportunity: their conquest of Axmure, their threat to Zenith and their past sack of Reikos. Each proposed mandate would have turned Imperial ruthlessness specifically against them.
n.Highguard: Highguard's assembly had upheld support for the Iron Helms as virtuous tools of cruelty. It could have made the Seventh Wave permanently vengeful in memory of the Druj sack of Reikos, but the resolution records no Highborn mandate taking effect.
n.Navarr: Navarr was one of the nations able to authorise a mandate for ruthless onslaught. Brat Umbral Path raised it, but the Navarri assembly did not uphold it.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are cited as claiming to rival Urizen in the arcane arts, yet falling short of the Citadel Guard's magical mastery.
n.Urizen: Urizen's assembly upheld Sophus Cascade's mandate to turn the Citadel Guard from cyclic magic to arcane mastery and its Storm of Curses. After the named priest Lucretius died, Zeno, Stallion's Sibling, declined to carry it out, so the change will not happen.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Iron Helms inspired the whole debate, and Varushka could authorise ruthless onslaught for its armies. Belakov Prochnost raised the mandate, but the assembly did not uphold it.

t.Reikos: The memory of the Druj sack and brutal occupation of Reikos, with its enslavement and experimentation, was the stated motive for offering the Seventh Wave the chance to become vengeful.
t.Semmerholm: Druj armies have conquered Axmure and threaten all of Semmerholm, with Dawnish manor houses burning. This fuelled the opportunity for the Eastern Sky to become bloodthirsty.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: The Barrens is not named; the page refers only to the Druj armies whose invasion prompted these opportunities.
t.Zenith: The Druj threat to Zenith's Halls of Knowledge, following the fall of Endsmeet, prompted the offer to give the Citadel Guard arcane mastery. The mandate was upheld but its priest declined to carry it out.

r.Semmerholm/Axmure: Axmure has been conquered by the Druj after the fall of the Towers of the Dawn and the Gate. This loss is cited as driving Dawnish soldiers' thirst for revenge.

Proud to serve.d: Heilyn named the Empire's greatest challenges as internal: threats to the unity of the faith, to trust between nations and to the economy. With the strategic mana fund severely reduced, individual mages and covens had paid for the border fortresses and several army enchantments; Heilyn thanked them, naming covens including the Saker, Skywise and Carta Notturno, and urged citizens to donate crystals. Acknowledging terrible magic used by the Empire, he swore to consult carefully and, if he supported action costing Imperial civilian lives, to submit himself to the affected nation's Senators and National Assembly. He stood by the military council's Mournwold decision and welcomed the new Conclave Order of the Silver Chalice under Raewynn Farkas.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the three external foes the Empire faces, which Heilyn set aside to speak of internal challenges.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the three external foes the Empire faces, which Heilyn set aside to speak of internal challenges.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: named as one of the three external foes the Empire faces, which Heilyn set aside to speak of internal challenges.
n.The Marches: The Warmage addressed the Mournwold, a Marcher territory, directly, saying he had seen first-hand what the military council's decision there cost and stood by it, while pledging to submit to the Senators and National Assembly of any nation bearing grave civilian losses from future strategic magic.

t.Mournwold: Heilyn acknowledged the heavy cost of the military council's strategy in the Mournwold, which he witnessed himself, and declared he stood by the decision though he would have preferred a better option.

Queens and kings.d: Solomon, the Archmage of Summer, had proposed a tourney to end Cathan Canae's blizzards over the Icy Crag. Barien organised a grand melee in the Dawnish Glory square, with each interested eternal sponsoring three champions. Eleonaris publicly rebuked Dawn for snubbing her herald and siding with Jaheris, and invited willing champions to her Marshal. Her champions won, and she became patron of the college; rival eternals accepted the result for now. Koboldi offered mine owners help expanding their mines in exchange for white granite and any non-magical finds. Arsenio Rezia di Tassato raised the required Declaration of Concord, so mines enchanted with Delve Deep, Beneath the Mountain could be upgraded using white granite that season.

n.Dawn: Eleonaris singled out Dawn for ignoring her herald and siding with the traitor Jaheris, while still calling on her Knights of Glory. She said she would judge the nation's heart by whether Dawnish champions stood forth for her, and her rebuke shocked many in Dawn's lands.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Eleonaris is noted to have been openly supportive of the Jotun orcs.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the opening scene shows Varushkan miners suspiciously hearing a koboldi foreman's offer on behalf of King Adamant, whom one of them briefly mistakes for Agramant.

t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova is not named. The page's only Varushkan link is a scene of Varushkan miners meeting koboldi, whose offer applied to mine owners across the Empire.

Rabbits and snares.d: Irra Harah answered Volfe of Ashenhall, Archmage of Spring, through a young Marcher-garbed briar. He agreed to parley around two on Saturday about the Mournwold, the Barrens and the tyrants of Asavea. He asked to hear from non-citizens, to meet Raewynn Farkas of the Navarr and Highborn Hazelelponi, and only then to speak briefly with the archmage. He would withdraw if the Imperial Warmage attended. The Lictors sent an engraved square of green iron accepting a formal parley at eleven on Friday night, and the civil service advised caution. Zakalwe declined a formal parley but would send representatives at five on Saturday. He asked that Vaan of the Auric Horizon attend so he could fulfil an obligation.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the state of the Barrens, then held by the Druj, is one of the subjects Irra Harah wishes to raise at his parley.
n.Navarr: Irra Harah specifically asked to meet Raewynn Farkas of the Navarr during his parley with the Empire.
n.The Marches: Irra Harah's messenger came dressed in Marcher garb, and the eternal wants to discuss the Mournwold. In the heralds' account, Dourfell keep has fallen and some of its people survive among the orcs.
n.Urizen: Zakalwe asked that Vaan of the Auric Horizon, a citizen of Urizen, be invited to the discussion so that the eternal can fulfil an unspecified obligation owed to him.

t.Mournwold: The Mournwold heads Irra Harah's parley agenda. His heralds speak of poison and curses there, and the Warmage would not promise that they would not be used again.
t.The Barrens: Irra Harah intends to discuss the state of the Barrens, then held by the Druj, at his Saturday parley with the Empire.

Recognise the House of Guiscard.d: Proposed by Segura and seconded by Skarsind, the motion formally announced Imperial support for the House of Guiscard, a house of the Iron Confederacy, in its bid to become rulers of Kalino. It followed a similar motion passed at the Summer Solstice 381YE. The motion passed. As a statement of the Senate's position it carried no legal force within the Empire, but it was noted that it might have diplomatic consequences in dealings with the Iron Confederacy.

t.Kalino: The Senate formally backed the House of Guiscard's claim to rule Kalino, then held by the Iron Confederacy, though the recognition carried no legal weight and only possible diplomatic consequences.

Research Mfanwy.d: Using the power to announce historical research delegated by the Senate, the Dredgemaster of Feverwater (also styled the Fevermaster of Dredgewater on the page) announced research into Myfanwy of Hercynia, covering her travels and her relationships with the First Empress. The commission cost 5 thrones, all of which were provided by Eleri Bronwen's Rest. The page states that research begins once the funds are provided; it does not record any findings.

n.Navarr: The research looks into a figure from Navarr's own Hercynian past, Myfanwy, and her links to the First Empress. Its 5-throne cost was met by Eleri Bronwen's Rest.

t.Hercynia: The territory gives Myfanwy of Hercynia her name, and she is the subject of the commissioned research into her travels and her relationships with the First Empress.

Seals and stars.d: Empty night skies persisted over much of the Empire, including Casinea where Anvil lies, so naga there and at the summit felt a strengthened urge towards secrecy. Skies were clear over Morrow, Spiral, Redoubt, Miekarova, Skarsind and Zenith, though a Penumbral Veil settled over Zenith again. Imperial citizens still could not draw on Spring regio, which made rituals such as Forge the Wooden Fastness impossible. Highguard's Blazing Sun coven raised two citadels, Wintermark's Sussivari Frost Coven raised four, and Urizen's Concordium of Pallas used a new ritual, The Immaculate Architect, to finish the Broken Ride fortification early. The hylje ended their raids and blessed Sermersuaq's farms and fleets.

n.Druj: The Druj were blamed, as Urizen saw it, for the renewed Penumbral Veil over Zenith, where Highborn armies were holding them back, and the stars stayed hidden over their Barrens.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the skies over Grendel-held Spiral were clear, and the Grendel were recalled as having enslaved Richard of Holberg when Evenstar fell.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Blazing Sun coven raised icy citadels in Clypion, aiding Highborn armies defending Zenith, and on Chalcis Mount in Reikos. Naga at Anvil in Highborn Casinea still felt the shroud's pull towards secrecy.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the night skies over Imperial Orc-held Skarsind were clear.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun-held Liathaven was among the territories still lacking stars.
n.Navarr: A Wintermark citadel of night magic protected the marshes of the Upper Tarn Valley in Navarr's Therunin. The loss of Spring regio still made rituals such as The Dance of Navarr and Thorn impossible.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: one of Richard of Holberg's past designs was a mithril dome in Segura that produced prismatic ink.
n.The League: A Sussivari citadel was raised in the Morass near Holberg, and Holberg-trained architect Richard agreed to design a mana structure for Tassato.
n.The Marches: Sussivari citadels guarded Ottermire and Grey Fens in Bregasland. Mournwold stayed starless but was chosen as one of the three sites for Richard of Holberg's mana structure designs.
n.Urizen: The Concordium of Pallas unveiled The Immaculate Architect to complete the Broken Ride fortification early. Zenith lost its empty sky but gained a new Penumbral Veil, and Morrow was chosen for one of Richard's mana structure designs.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the night skies over Varushkan Miekarova were clear.
n.Wintermark: The hylje ended their raids and blessed Sermersuaq, bringing bonus production to Wintermark farms and fleets there, while the Sussivari Frost Coven raised four citadels across the Empire. Sesi of the Suaq received a mysterious seal-folk gift he wished to discuss with his tradition.

t.Bregasland: Wintermark's Sussivari Frost Coven raised citadels of mist and night in both Ottermire and Grey Fens to guard Bregasland.
t.Casinea: Casinea remained under the starless shroud, so naga at Anvil felt their urge towards subtlety and secrecy strengthen, though the sky directly over Anvil appeared normal.
t.Holberg: A Sussivari citadel was raised in the Morass, and Holberg's university was named as where Richard of Holberg trained as a magician-architect.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven was listed among the adjacent territories whose skies remained empty of stars.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: the night skies over Miekarova were clear.
t.Morrow: Morrow's skies were clear, and the Conclave chose it as one of three territories for which Richard of Holberg would design a mana structure.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold's skies stayed empty of stars, but it was chosen as a site for one of Richard of Holberg's mana structure designs.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt's skies were clear, and the fall of its spire of Evenstar to the Grendel was recalled as the place of Richard's capture.
t.Reikos: A Highborn icy citadel was raised on Chalcis Mount, and the Immaculate Architect ritual let the Broken Ride fortification be finished well ahead of schedule.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Richard of Holberg once designed a mithril dome over a granite structure in Segura that yielded prismatic ink.
t.Sermersuaq: The hylje left Atkonaroq and blessed Sermersuaq with full nets, plentiful game and safe passages, a blessing expected to continue through Winter.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the night skies over Skarsind were clear.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the night skies over Spiral were clear.
t.Tassato: The Conclave chose Tassato as one of three territories for which Richard of Holberg would design a mana structure.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens were listed among the adjacent territories whose skies remained starless.
t.Therunin: The Sussivari Frost Coven invoked the power of night to raise a protective citadel amid the marshes of the Upper Tarn Valley.
t.Zenith: The empty sky lifted over Zenith but a Penumbral Veil settled again, which Urizen blamed on the Druj, while a Highborn citadel in Clypion aided the armies defending it.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised a citadel of coiling mist, shadow and night magic in Grey Fens.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: A Wintermark citadel of night magic was raised in Ottermire to protect against the Empire's enemies.
r.Holberg/The Morass: The Sussivari Frost Coven conjured a citadel of mist and shadow in the Morass near Holberg.
r.Reikos/Broken Ride: The Concordium of Pallas used The Immaculate Architect to fit six months of work into twelve weeks, completing the grand fortification early.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: The Blazing Sun coven raised an icy citadel on Chalcis Mount to guard the slow rebuilding against surprise invasion.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: A Sussivari citadel of night magic was raised amid the marshes of the Upper Tarn Valley.
r.Zenith/Clypion: The Blazing Sun coven raised an icy citadel in Clypion to help Highborn armies protect Zenith against the Druj.

The art of restraining power.d: Sumaah recognised the virtue of Bonewall Rek and Cole and invited them to Timoj; Rek sailed for Zemeh, and the Senate later accepted a Sumaah ceasefire. Asavea completed the Temple of the Way in Nemoria and sent white granite to Sarvos, leaving the liaison's appointment method to Maher i Zaydan i Riqueza. The Black Sails Quay ended high liao prices. Axou priests of the Order of the Ivory Cup lectured widely, provoking hostility. Jarm favoured Vezak while Kavor and Rigia cooled. Faraden welcomed the King's Stoke hub. Sarcophan herb surpluses ended, Commonwealth relations stayed cool, and Otkodov recognised Ambassador Juha the Cavespider as Skogr freed fifty slaves.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: rumour says Faraden advisor Lady Saretta favours a trade enclave in Dawn similar to the one planned for Upwold.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Imperial fleets have no opportunity to trade with the Druj this season.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan merchants make no secret of an orc embassy in the Delves, and rumours claim they sell Imperial goods in Dubhtraig.
n.Highguard: Highborn of Felix's Watch helped the Sumaah inquisition pass smoothly at Anvil. Necropolis's Black Sails Quay normalised liao prices and its Chantry of the Silver Skull hosted Axou lecturers.
n.Imperial Orcs: Sumaah formally recognised the virtue of Bonewall Rek and Bonewall Cole, and Rek set sail for Zemeh on his way to address the assemblies in Timoj. Separately, Axou visitors declined an invitation to the Legion's Rookery in Skarsind.
n.Navarr: Axou priests lectured at Bronwen's Rest Wayhouse in Therunin, where one visiting priest was afterwards struck by a curse of swarming insects.
n.The Brass Coast: Maher i Zaydan i Riqueza must decide how the Nemoria temple liaison is appointed. Antonio i Carno i Guerra's Gloaming Road is in demand as blight ravages Faraden gloaming.
n.The League: Sarvos received the first Asavean white granite. Axou priests lectured in Tassato, where students pelted them, and Faraden merchants praised the Blood Red Roads and mooted mercenary markets in Tassato and Temeschwar.
n.The Marches: The Senate-approved Faraden trade hub at King's Stoke in Upwold was widely welcomed, with the Court of the Five Winds eager for Marcher grain, fruit and alcohol, though work has yet to begin.
n.Thule: Thule recognised Ambassador Juha the Cavespider, and their emissary moved to Coldmere. Skogr the Red freed fifty Imperial slaves under a ransom agreement with Wintermark and plans to send traders to the Varushkan Winter Market.
n.Varushka: The Embassy to Otkodov in Miekarova was completed and the Thule emissary relocated to Coldmere. Axou priests lectured at the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, and Skogr the Red plans to trade at the Winter Market.
n.Wintermark: A ransom agreement with the people of Wintermark secured the release of fifty Imperial slaves held by Skogr the Red. Sarcophan traders also ventured towards Hahnmark to sell healing supplies to the grimnir.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan traders are a common sight around the Bay of Catazar.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: a band of Sarcophan traders reportedly made a speculative journey to Hahnmark to sell herbs and healing supplies to the grimnir.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the University of Holberg issued an informal invitation to the visiting Axou scholars.
t.Miekarova: The Embassy to Otkodov was completed here and the Thule emissary Rak relocated, grudgingly, to Coldmere. Axou priests also lectured at the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun.
t.Necropolis: The completed Black Sails Quay gave Axou merchants reliable access to liao, ending inflated prices. The Sumaah embassy buzzed with gossip about the orc doctrines, and Axou priests lectured at the Chantry of the Silver Skull.
t.Otkodov: The orcs of Otkodov grudgingly recognised Ambassador Juha the Cavespider. The Dragons remain keen to join the northern trade network and to acquire the remnants of the Runeforge beneath Gildenheim.
t.Sarvos: The first shipments of Asavean white granite arrived at the Sarvos docks after the Cavabianca Dock affair was resolved, and the Diora University invited Axou scholars to speak.
t.Segura: Faraden merchant families want the Blood Red Roads extended to Anduz, in Segura, and have reportedly been negotiating an offer of cheap white granite for such a project.
t.Sermersuaq: Red-cloaked Thule orcs escorted fifty freed Imperial slaves, provisioned to reach Atalaq, to the foothills of the Silver Peaks under a ransom agreement with Wintermark.
t.Skarsind: Some of the freed slaves had been taken during the recent invasion of Skarsind. The Axou declined an invitation to the Legion's Rookery, while Sarcophan traders journeyed here to sell to orc bonesetters.
t.Tassato: Axou priests lectured at the Printers' Guild Museum of Wonders, and School of Epistemology students pelted two of them with rotten vegetables and eggs. Faraden merchants talk of a future mercenary market here.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: there is talk of a Faraden mercenary market in Temeschwar once the enclaves are complete.
t.Therunin: Axou priests lectured at Bronwen's Rest Wayhouse, and afterwards one of them was subjected to a curse of swarming insects; the priests cooperated with magistrates and pressed charges where appropriate.
t.Upwold: The Senate approved a Faraden trade hub at King's Stoke, welcomed as a sign of expanding Faraden presence. Work has not yet begun, though granite is already stockpiled in Anduz.

r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: The fifty slaves freed by Skogr the Red were given furs, boots and enough food and water to reach Atalaq.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Thule orcs released fifty Imperial slaves in the foothills of the Silver Peaks, some of them captured during earlier Thule aggression in the region.
r.Upwold/Tower March: King's Stoke was chosen by the Senate as the site of a Faraden trade hub, though construction has yet to begin.

The mother of morality.d: Wintermark's condemnation by Ylmiska Ferbow and Gunnbrand Ironwill meant the Iron Helms would be shunned by Wintermark armies. The Helms then left the west for Sarvos, presumably to face the Grendel or the Druj. Three opportunities followed. Wintermark could urge its warriors to face the Jotun with respect, winning more victories but inflicting fewer casualties. The Freeborn could make the Red Wind Corsairs a Daring army that captures and ransoms enemies. The League could shun the Helms, or also let the Wolves of War take the physick quality. Gunnbrand Ironwill carried Wintermark's mandate and Gonzalo i Riqueza the Freeborn one. The resolution records no League mandate.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the departing Iron Helms were thought to be heading through Sarvos to face either the Grendel or the Druj.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Helms were thought to be heading east to face the Grendel or the Druj, and a recent Red Wind and Wolves of War raid on Grendel wealth in Spiral was cited as an example.
n.Jotun: Driven from the Mourne in part by the Iron Helms' butchery, the Jotun will for a year face Wintermark armies fighting for heroic victory rather than slaughter. These armies inflict fewer casualties but gain more victory points, which some mystics hoped might restore the old mutual respect between the two peoples.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr apothecaries were among those the Wolves of War might have recruited had the League taken the physick mandate.
n.The League: The League assembly's narrowly passed condemnation of the Iron Helms opened mandates to shun them or to give the Wolves of War the physick quality. The resolution records no League mandate being taken, so these opportunities were lost.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Helms' butchery took place in the Marcher territory of the Mournwold, from which the Jotun fled.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: in Emperor Guntherm's reign, Wintermark and Jotun warriors briefly joined forces to fight the Thule.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's priests shunned the Iron Helms, and Gunnbrand Ironwill was sent to urge the Mark's warriors to face the Jotun as heroes. Until Autumn 382YE, Wintermark armies fighting the Jotun gain more victory points but inflict fewer casualties.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Imperatrix Lisabetta is noted as a daughter of Holberg, and Holberg physicks were among those the Wolves of War might have recruited.
t.Mournwold: The Iron Helms' cruelty here helped drive the Jotun from the Mourne, a victory some Wintermark mystics called hollow and whose consequences cannot be undone.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the shunned Iron Helms left the west and headed to Sarvos, presumably on their way to face the Grendel or the Druj.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Red Wind Corsairs' and Wolves of War's recent raid on enemy wealth in Spiral was cited as proof of the profit in war without butchery.

The parents of security.d: Plans by Francesca di Sarvos for a Sarvos Arsenal and Dockyard were found at Diora University. The Arsenal would be a great port and shipyard, and would let the League maintain a navy while it held Cigno; it could be commissioned until the end of the Winter Solstice. Menno Van Ritsjhof designed a fortification of walls and granite-anchored chains that remains available. A mandate condemning the Iron Helms, who were already unpopular after a brawl, would have boosted League armies' resupply and cut Varushkan resupply, but it lapsed. About two-thirds of the College orcs, facing prejudice, moved to Skarsind and bonded to the Imperial Orc egregore as the liberated.

n.Grendel: Their sack of Sarvos lies behind both building proposals: the Arsenal could support a navy to repay their sneak attack, and the fortification was meant to stop any future seaborne invasion. Fear of Grendel infiltrators also fed suspicion of the College orcs.
n.Imperial Orcs: About two-thirds of the orcs educated at the College of the Liberated moved to Skarsind and bonded to the Imperial Orc egregore, where they are known as the liberated.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Freeborn are named as the Empire's foremost seafarers, and the Arsenal was pitched as a way for the League to become their naval equal.
n.The League: The League was offered a Naval Arsenal and its own navy, a great fortification for Sarvos, and a chance to strengthen citizen support for its armies. The Senate and the League Assembly took none of them, and the army-support opportunity was lost.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: stories of atrocities committed by the Iron Helms in the Mournwold circulated in Sarvos.
n.Varushka: The Iron Helms, wintering in Sarvos, gained a probably unjust reputation for savagery and anti-orc bigotry. A mandate that would have reduced Varushkan armies' resupply in League territories was never raised.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the fortification's designer, Menno Van Ritsjhof, is described as perhaps the most skilled siege architect in Holberg.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is named, alongside Siroc, as the place people think of when they think of Imperial shipping.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: tales of Iron Helms atrocities in the Mournwold fuelled hostility towards them in Sarvos.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos could gain a Naval Arsenal and Dockyard, open to commission until the end of the Winter Solstice, and a fortification of walls and chains that can still be commissioned. Neither was commissioned that season, while tensions over the College orcs and the Iron Helms grew in the city.
t.Skarsind: Most of the College-educated Jarmish orcs settled here, taking mine work and business roles such as those tied to Torfast Trading Post, and bonded to the Imperial Orc egregore.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: grumbling citizens of Sarvos suggested the Iron Helms might be happier in Temeschwar.

r.Sarvos/Bocche: The proposed fortification would resist any Shore Offensive in Bocche with an effective strength of 3,000.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: A League navy raised through the Arsenal could be supported only while Cigno stayed under League control. The proposed fortification would defend Cigno against shore offensives with an effective strength of 6,000.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: The proposed fortification would resist any Shore Offensive in Uccelini with an effective strength of 3,000.
r.Skarsind/Southpine: Mentioned in passing: Southpine is not named; it is linked through the liberated orcs settling across Skarsind in its mines and businesses.

The place you called home.d: Refused a homeland, the orcs ceremonially cast aside their war spears, though about half kept their arms as the Spears of the Pines. Navarr generals fighting in Therunin or the Barrens may call on them as a 1,000-strong force. Chief Vallack became their liaison to the Military Council and promised a map of the Mallum. The Senate approved their weirwood fortification, the Holt of the Oak, and let them run the Thimble for four wains of weirwood a season. It also redirected the Gardens of High Chalcis' herbs to them, while the Navarr Assembly urged Therunin to share herbs. Volfe of Ashenhall had a Rivers of Life ritual text given to their magicians.

n.Druj: The Druj drove the Great Forest Orcs from the Barrens and still hold their weirwood groves. The orcs promised the Empire maps of the Mallum and what they know of Druj armies, though Vallack warned the information is years out of date.
n.Highguard: Highborn were offered ways to aid the orcs through Reikos, whose people share their experience of Druj oppression. The Senate chose to redirect the bounty of the Gardens of High Chalcis to the orcs for a year.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs are said to be cordial to Imperial Orcs and treat them as equals.
n.Navarr: The Navarr gained orc neighbours in Therunin, and Navarr generals can call on the Spears of the Pines in Therunin or the Barrens. The Navarr Assembly charged Tynan Lonestriker to urge Therunin's people to share herbs, and the Navarr custodian of the Thimble will receive four fewer wains of weirwood each season.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the civil service remarked that the orcs were hardly likely to become the equal of the Urizen in magic within a few years.

t.Reikos: The Senate redirected the herbs of the Gardens of High Chalcis to the Great Forest Orcs, so the great work will give Reikos' herb garden owners no benefit for the next year.
t.The Barrens: This was the orcs' lost homeland, now in Druj hands, which they hope one day to retake. Any Navarr army fighting to conquer it may call the Spears of the Pines to its side.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest Orcs now live throughout Therunin's non-vallorn regions as guests, and their warriors guard against the forest's beasts. If Tynan provides the liao for the Navarr mandate, its herb gardens and businesses will give up part of their output to aid the orcs.

r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The orcs once tended valuable weirwood groves here and speak fondly of them, but the groves now lie in Druj hands.
r.Therunin/Greenheart: Mentioned in passing: being occupied by the vallorn, it is one of the two regions the orcs will not spread into.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: This is the centre of the orcs' settlement and home of the Great Forest Encampment where Chief Vallack can be reached. The Senate approved the orc-garrisoned weirwood fortification, the Holt of the Oak, to be built here.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Mentioned in passing: being occupied by the vallorn, it is one of the two regions the orcs will not spread into.

Unable to see.d: At the Summer Solstice 381YE the General Assembly condemned Yael for preaching the rejected doctrine of The Beyond, and the magistrates executed her when she refused clemency. The Highborn Assembly had earlier endorsed her as the First Empress Reborn, so Highborn grief was marked more by sorrow than by rage. The schism worsened, and penalties on Highborn armies fighting alongside other forces rose to 60% for military units and 25% for armies. Two paths were offered: a Highborn mandate to disavow Yael, or a General Assembly change of doctrine accepting the Land Without Tears, backed by a mandate to embrace it. The Highborn Assembly supported Melchior of Adina's Charge's conciliatory mandate, and with 250 liao he set out to return Highguard to orthodoxy.

n.Highguard: Highguard grieved its executed daughter and saw its armies suffer growing penalties when fighting beside other nations, until its Assembly chose Melchior's mandate to turn the nation back from Yael's teachings towards orthodoxy.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr Assembly is cited as having utterly rejected Yael's claim to be the First Empress reborn.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Marches are not named directly, and the only nearby reference is to the troubled situation in the Mournwold, used as a comparison.

t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the out-of-character notes compare the Yael schism to the similarly complex and strife-filled situation in the Mournwold.

Workers in struggle.d: The civil service estimated the new Delver of the Depths title would yield 50 weltsilver, 20 tempest jade and 12 crystal mana each season. The scholar Peter of Hintown offered to explore the sinkhole's tunnels for 5 Thrones if invited. In Serra Briante, orcs stole four wains of mithril, cutting the Great Mine's yield to 18 wains this season, before it went to auction. The militia captured one orc and a herald serving an unnamed Summer eternal. A huge marshwalker, possibly linked to the Druj, attacked the Feverwater dredgers near Black Sails steading. Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar bought the naming rights, and Tobrytan Dunning sent Peter on his expedition.

n.Druj: The marshwalker attack on the Feverwater dredgers was suspected to be Druj work, since they are known to use such creatures and half the Feverwater lies in the Mallum.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs are not named; the mithril heist is attributed only to an unidentified gang of orcs.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the orc thieves were thought to have fled into the mountains, possibly reaching Jotun-held Liathaven.
n.Navarr: The Navarr egregore reported a Sentinel Gate conjunction that let up to thirty citizens reach Black Sails steading, where a marshwalker had killed dredgers and threatened the steading.
n.The Brass Coast: The Great Mine of Briante lost four wains of mithril to an orc raid, and the Freeborn egregore offered a Sentinel Gate route for five people to help the Serra Briante militia investigate.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Tobrytan Dunning became Delver of the Depths and funded Peter of Hintown and his Winterfolk companions to explore the sinkhole beside New Dunhall.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark, whose Dunhearth Hall lands were badly hit by the sinkhole, became the base for Peter of Hintown's authorised expedition into the newly named "Lorenzo's Deep Pockets".
t.Kahraman: Orcs raided mithril wagons from the Great Mine of Briante in Kahraman, stealing four wains and reducing the mine's output this season.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the orc thieves were believed to have possibly fled into Jotun-held Liathaven.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is not named; the sinkhole is described only as lying in the north-western Empire.

r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: New Dunhall in Wood Heath was where the Delver of the Depths had to send a winged messenger authorising Peter of Hintown's expedition.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Mentioned in passing: the regular patrols from the garrison at Fort Braydon raised the question of how the orcs reached the mine and escaped unseen.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: The Great Mine in Serra Briante lost four wains of mithril to an orc heist, and its militia captured one orc and a Summer herald while investigating.
